subject: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos@novasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers

Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for the time on Friday — great signal that Nova is ready to consolidate multiple ingestion pipelines into a single inference tier. Per our discussion, I attached a concise workbook that outlines three annual commit packages (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) and a short "accelerator" option that provides temporary credits to smooth the ramp.

Highlights in the attachment:
- Starter: 250M token annual commit, lower entry monthly billing, 10% discount on hosted per-token rates.
- Growth: 1.5B token annual commit, steeper per-token discount (20%), two-stage ramp with mid-year true-up.
- Enterprise: 6B token commit, 30% discount, SLA-backed latency tier and dedicated capacity option (optional add-on).
- Accelerator: up to 200M token credits available in Q1 to offset marketing-driven spike; credits convert to committed tokens if consumed.

A few important terms to note in the workbook: billing cadence (monthly invoicing against committed token burn), fallback pricing for overage, and a flexible window for mid-year commit top-ups (desktop true-up). We also call out an optional performance SLA for Enterprise commitments and a 45-day termination notice with pro-rated refunds for unused prepayments.

Can you confirm: 1) your preferred commit tier (Starter/Growth/Enterprise), 2) whether Nova needs burst capacity in Q1, and 3) if procurement needs a PO before legal reviews the SOW? Once you confirm, Ben and I will produce a compact SOW and pricing appendix.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attach: 20270118-redwood-annual-commit-accelerator.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)

From: Carlos Reyes <carlos@novasystems.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers

Olga,

Appreciate the clear options and the workbook. A few quick questions from my side — procurement and engineering are already looped in but asked me to confirm:

1) For Growth vs Enterprise, is the SLA (latency target) included or is that an add-on? We operate a low-latency product and need the 95th percentile token latency to be under 120ms.
2) How strict is the annual true-up? If we underuse in H1 because of a delayed feature launch, can we shift commit between quarters or is it locked to calendar months?
3) The accelerator credit — does it convert to committed volume (counted toward threshold) or is it separate promotional credit?

Also, our CFO has asked for an example invoice cadence showing how monthly billing vs prepayment would look for Growth. Can you send an example?

Thanks,
Carlos
VP Product — Nova Systems

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos@novasystems.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers

Carlos — thanks for the questions, great ones. Short answers before I attach the example invoice and a one-page SLA summary:

1) SLA: For Enterprise, the latency SLA (95th <= 120ms) is included when you opt into the dedicated capacity add-on. Growth tier can get a soft SLA (target) but it's not financially-backed unless you move to the dedicated Enterprise option. We include an automated fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity is constrained, but that doesn't carry a latency credit.

2) True-up flexibility: The Growth plan includes a mid-year true-up window to shift committed tokens across quarters (up to 20% shift) to accommodate delayed launches. Larger shifts require a short amendment but are common — we can bake that into the SOW.

3) Accelerator credit: Promotional credits are applied first to the monthly invoice; if consumed, they do count toward the annual committed burn for threshold calculations (i.e., they will after consumption reduce your effective net overage). That ensures you can spike without immediate overage exposure.

Attached: sample invoice cadence (mock numbers) and SLA-onepager. For the invoice cadence, we show two options: monthly invoicing against commit with a quarterly true-up, or an upfront prepay with monthly burn reporting and pro-rated credits for underuse.

Next step: Olga — can you share the SOW skeleton and a short comparison table mapping feature flags to tiers (KV cache, prefix caching, dedicated pool, priority routing)? Carlos — if the Enterprise latency SLA is a blocker, we can show a short bench test and a commit ramp that includes an initial probation window (30 days) to validate latencies.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attach: example-invoice-growth.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB); SLA-onepager.pdf (doc, 12 KB)

From: Carlos Reyes <carlos@novasystems.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers

Ben / Olga — that all looks reasonable. Procurement confirmed they prefer monthly invoicing against the commit with a quarterly true-up (option A), and they'd like the accelerator credits to count toward the burn (good to hear). A few follow-ups from finance:

• Can you split Growth pricing into committed per-token rate and a separate overage rate (we'd like clear visibility into marginal cost if we spike).
• We'd like a 60-day PO lead time before the first invoice if we need to route through our enterprise purchasing system.
• Are there any minimum usage floors inside a year (besides the annual commit)? For example, if we sign Growth but only burn 850M of the 1.5B commit, will there be an automatic conversion to Starter-level pricing or will we owe the difference?

If you can send a redlineable SOW and a 1-page summary for procurement that lays out these three billing rules, I can route to our legal and procurement teams.

Thanks,
Carlos

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos@novasystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit & accelerator offer — Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers

Carlos — thanks, and great direction from procurement. Attached is a compact redlineable SOW (PDF), a 1-page procurement summary, and a small table that separates committed rate vs overage rate for Growth (committed: $0.00065 / token, overage: $0.00110 / token) — numbers in the table are illustrative and we can lock them in with the term sheet.

Key clarifications in the procurement summary:
- Accelerator credits: counted toward committed burn once consumed; they do not auto-convert to a non-refundable prepayment unless you choose to convert them explicitly.
- Underuse: if actual annual burn < commit at year-end, you pay the committed shortfall (standard approach). We include a one-time grace of up to 10% for Growth during year one to accommodate delayed launches; the grace is waived in year two unless renegotiated.
- PO lead time: we can accept a 60-day PO lead time; first invoice will be scheduled after PO receipt and activation.

Next steps: 1) I will attach the redline SOW and procurement summary now (sent). 2) If procurement/legal want edits, send their redlines; Marissa will run the SOW changes and coordinate final countersign. 3) If you want the dedicated Enterprise latency SLA validated, Ben can schedule a 2-week bench test with our infra team.

If this sounds good, I'll turn the workbook into a neat pricing appendix and update the Drive folder with a pre-approved clause set for procurement.

Best,
Olga
Attach: SOW-novasystems-draft-2027-01.pdf (doc, 110 KB); procurement-summary-novasystems.pdf (doc, 6 KB)
